measurement: Rust cibersort stage (iobrx/fast/cibersort_fast.py::cibersort_fast): thread scaling + cold-start characterization
input: testdata/eset_stad_symbol.parquet (50181x10) + LM22 (547x22), common=531, perm=100, QN=True, absolute=False, DataFrame-in (no CSV)

code_facts.rayon_pool: A fresh rayon::ThreadPoolBuilder().num_threads(n).build() is constructed inside EVERY cibersort_core call (iobrx/crates/iobrx_rust/src/lib.rs:1032-1035); there is no persistent global pool, so every per-call time below already includes 224-thread pool construction.
code_facts.blas_pinning: cibersort_fast._init_blas() pins numpy's bundled openblas to 1 thread (avoids oversubscription from inside rayon workers); it dlopens scipy/numpy openblas .so via ctypes once per process and passes kernel addresses to the Rust module.

1_thread_scaling.protocol: fresh subprocess per thread count; 1 warmup + 3 reps of the full perm=100 call; perf_counter wall; median reported

2_cold_process_start.protocol: fresh `python3 -c` subprocess per run (3 runs); child perf_counter splits; parent measures total spawn-to-exit wall; first call = perm=100, n_threads=224

summary.note: cold start to first-result ~= 3.1s total; import of the compiled module is ~0.4ms; the first call itself is within ~0.1-0.3s of the warm in-process median

3_rayon_pool_first_vs_later_calls.protocol: fresh subprocess; 3 consecutive timed cibersort_fast calls (perm=100, n_threads=224)
3_rayon_pool_first_vs_later_calls.finding: No persistent pool to warm: the pool is rebuilt inside every call. The one-time first-call penalty (fully cold: 4.00s vs 2.59/2.74s later) is almost entirely cold-cache/page-fault cost, NOT pool spin-up and NOT init: _init_blas costs 3.8ms and the LM22 read 15.8ms. Post-init first call is 2.81s vs 2.39/2.52s later, i.e. a residual ~0.3-0.4s first-touch cost.

5_memory_peak_rss.finding: Process peak RSS (534 MiB) is set by the numpy/pandas/pyarrow import phase; the cibersort stage never raises it at any thread count. Steady-state cost of the call itself: +277 MiB at 224 threads (~1.24 MiB/thread, faulted-in rayon worker stacks + per-fit buffers) vs +9.5 MiB VmHWM at 1 thread.
